title: Base change for $Rf_!$ on the localizing category
statement:
Work in the standing scheme setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: fix a prime $\ell$ and a
field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$; all schemes are separated and of finite
type over $k$, and all morphisms are $k$-morphisms. Let $\Lambda$ be an admissible coefficient
in the sense of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type and
let $v:Y'\to Y$ be a morphism in this setting (so $Y'$ is a standing scheme), with $Y'$ qcqs.
Form the cartesian square with $f':X'=X\times_YY'\to Y'$ and $u:X'\to X$. For a
compactification $f=p\circ j$, $j:X\to\overline X$, let $f'=p'\circ j'$ be its base
change, with $v':\overline X'=\overline X\times_YY'\to\overline X$. Then:

1. there is a canonical isomorphism $v'^*j_!\simeq j'_!u^*$ of functors
$D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)\to D(\overline X'_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$;
2. the composite
$\beta:v^*Rp_*j_!\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rp'_*v'^*j_!\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rp'_*j'_!u^*$
of proper base change and (1) is an isomorphism of functors
$\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))\to\Loc(\Dctf(Y',\Lambda))$;
3. $\beta$ is compatible with the comparison isomorphisms between
compactifications of $f$ and of $f'$.

proof.text: The pulled-back factorization is a compactification by [lemma-nagata-compactification-base-change]; in particular $j'$ is quasi-compact open and $p'$ is proper. For an open immersion, module extension by zero is additive and exact by [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek] and is left adjoint to module pullback by [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek-adjunction]. Module pullback is exact by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. Use the module pullback/direct-image adjunctions of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. On an object $V\to X$, the two sheaf functors $u_*j'^*$ and $j^*v'_*$ evaluate a sheaf $M$ on the same object $V\times_X X'=V\times_{\overline X}\overline X'$: open restriction is site localization by [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization](1), and direct image is evaluation on the fibre product by [def-sfb-finite-lower-star]. The identification respects the coefficient actions because module direct image has precisely that underlying sheaf with action through the canonical coefficient map [def-sfb-module-lower-star]. Hence $u_*j'^*\simeq j^*v'_*$ naturally. The composite-adjunction formula [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] makes $v'^*j_!$ and $j'_!u^*$ left adjoints to these identified functors. The unit-compatible isomorphism between them exists by [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation]; denote it $O_c$. Since all these left adjoints are exact, the same isomorphism applies termwise to complexes and descends through quasi-isomorphisms, as in [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. This proves (1). Its restriction to $X'$ is the identity of $u^*K$: the open unit is the canonical $j^*j_!\simeq\mathrm{id}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], and the common-right-adjoint identification on an object over $X'$ is the identity fibre-product identification. The unit equation characterizing $O_c$ therefore restricts to the identity. The ringed-site formulation applies to the internal module objects by [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], with coefficients identified by the Cartesian coefficient theorem.

source.place: Clause (1): common right adjoint, exact descent, and open-unit normalization

proof.text: All schemes in the compactifications and their pullbacks are in the standing setting, so both $p$ and $p'$ are proper between standing schemes. By [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-pullback], $v^*,u^*,v'^*$ preserve $\Dctf$, direct sums and the localizing closures. By [det-proper-image-localizing-open], $j_!K\in\Loc(\Dctf(\overline X,\Lambda))$ when $K\in\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$. Apply [det-sf-comp-coherence-single] to $c=(j,p)$ and to its base change $c'=(j',p')$. Together with the pullback statement this puts $v^*Rp_*j_!$ and $Rp'_*j'_!u^*$ in $\Loc(\Dctf(Y',\Lambda))$; (1) identifies the latter with $Rp'_*v'^*j_!$. This uses the stated conclusions of those nodes, not the proof of an extension node. On $\Dctf(\overline X,\Lambda)$, the canonical proper base-change map is invertible by [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-finite](2) for finite $\Lambda$, [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-integral](3) for $\mathcal O_E$, and [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-rational](3) for $E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Here $\Dctf\subset\Dbc$ by definition, so the integral and rational clauses apply; $\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathbf Q_\ell$ are the cases $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. The standing assumption on $Y'$ also permits the proper-image input for $p'$ in the integral theorem. By [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-extension] the same map is invertible on $\Loc(\Dctf(\overline X,\Lambda))$. Evaluate it on $j_!K$ and compose with $Rp'_*O_c$ to obtain the isomorphism $\beta_c$ of (2).

source.place: Clause (2): stated localizing targets and coefficient-level base change extended to the localizing closure

proof.text:
Fix the following comparison conventions on the ordinary unbounded module-object derived categories. The adjunction $a^*\dashv Ra_*$ is [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], since pullback is exact by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. For a Cartesian square with vertical map $a$ and horizontal maps $b,b_1$, write $B_a:b^*Ra_*\to Ra'_*b_1^*$ for the mate of the canonical pullback square isomorphism $a'^*b^*\simeq b_1^*a^*$. In components this is $Ra'_*b_1^*\varepsilon_a\circ Ra'_*(\theta Ra_*)\circ\eta_{a'}b^*Ra_*$, exactly the unit/square/counit formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Thus this notation specifies the same canonical map used in step 2 for every coefficient, without passing to a completed category. The pullback compositions are those of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], applied termwise. Their associativity can be checked before localization: both parenthesizations use the same iterated fibre product and the coefficient balancing map $((m\otimes a)\otimes b)\otimes c\mapsto m\otimes abc$. Use the canonical $R(ab)_*\simeq Ra_*Rb_*$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], transported to internal modules by [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. These comparisons are the conjugates of pullback composition under the derived adjunctions: a K-injective $I$ remains K-injective under each direct image by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] and exactness of pullback, so the normalization in the composition node can use the identity resolution of $b_*I$. Both successive comparison routes are then the same sectionwise composition isomorphism. To check the adjunction normalization, write the two derived Hom adjunctions for a composite $ab$: they send $\operatorname{Hom}(b^*a^*M,N)$ first to $\operatorname{Hom}(a^*M,Rb_*N)$ and then to $\operatorname{Hom}(M,Ra_*Rb_*N)$. On a K-injective representative these are the underived module-complex Hom bijections modulo homotopy, whose composite is the Hom bijection for $ab$ by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] and the underived composition adjunction of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. The identity on a left adjoint determines its unit, and the identity on a right adjoint determines its counit under these bijections, so the units and counits agree with the composite ones. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2),(3) gives, in these canonical composition coordinates,
$$B_{ab}=(Ra'_*B_b)\circ(B_aRb_*).$$
This is an equality of actual natural transformations, including their units and counits, rather than an identification of abstract isomorphic functors.

source.place: Clause (3): unit/square/counit construction and the proper-composition pasting used below

proof.text: Let $c_a=(j_a:X\hookrightarrow Z_a,p_a:Z_a\to Y)$, $a=1,2$, be arbitrary compactifications of $f$, and put $F_c=Rp_*j_!$. Choose a common scheme-theoretically dense refinement $d=(j_d:X\hookrightarrow D,q:D\to Y)$ with maps $h_a:D\to Z_a$ by [det-nagata-refinement-common-dense]. Let primes denote base change along $v$. Do not assume that $d'$ or $c_a'$ is dense. Apply the finite-family clause of the same node to $c_1',c_2',d'$ to obtain a scheme-theoretically dense compactification $d''=(j'':X'\hookrightarrow W,r:W\to Y')$, with refinements $k:W\to D'$ and $k_a:W\to Z_a'$. Both $h'_ak$ and $k_a$ are $Y'$-morphisms from $W$ to $Z_a'$ extending the given map on $X'$. Since the source $d''$ is scheme-theoretically dense, [det-nagata-refinement-morphisms](3) gives $h'_ak=k_a$. Every cited compactification open is quasi-compact. The bases $Y,Y'$ are qcqs by the statement and standing setting, as required by the common-dense-refinement node. For a refinement $h$ with dense source, even if its target is not dense, apply [det-sf-comp-composition-interchange](2),(3) with $p=\mathrm{id}$, $i$ the target open, and $r=h$. This supplies $e_h:j_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_*j_{\mathrm{source}!}K$ on the localizing domain, uniquely normalized to identity on the open. Define $\rho_h=Rp_*e_h$ followed by the inverse proper-composition comparison of step 3. The compactification comparisons of [det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle] are therefore computed as $\phi_{c_2,c_1}=\rho_{h_2}^{-1}\rho_{h_1}$, and after base change as $\phi_{c_2',c_1'}=\rho_{k_2}^{-1}\rho_{k_1}$. All refinements for which an $e$ or $\rho$ is used here have dense source $d$ or $d''$, not the possibly nondense $d'$.

source.place: Clause (3): dense replacement of all pulled-back compactifications and identification of refinement maps

proof.text:
Write $v_a:Z_a'\to Z_a$ and $w:D'\to D$ for the projections, and let $O_a:v_a^*j_{a!}\simeq j'_{a!}u^*$ and $O_d:w^*j_{d!}\simeq j'_{d!}u^*$ be step 1. For fixed $a$ and $K$, consider the two maps into $Rk_{a*}j''_!u^*K$, using $h'_ak=k_a$ and the proper-composition coordinates of step 3:
$$
L_a=e_{k_a,u^*K}\circ O_a,
$$
$$
M_a=Rh'_{a*}(e_{k,u^*K})\circ Rh'_{a*}(O_d)\circ B_{h_a,j_{d!}K}\circ v_a^*(e_{h_a,K}).
$$
Both have source $v_a^*j_{a!}K\simeq j'_{a!}u^*K$. Here $u^*K$ lies in the required localizing category by [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-pullback]. Check the open restriction explicitly. A refinement has inverse image of $X$ equal to its source open and is identity there. For an object $V\to X$, [def-sfb-finite-lower-star] and [def-sfb-module-lower-star] give $(h_*I)(V)=I(V\times_{Z_a}D)=I(V)$ with the same module action. Open restriction is site localization by [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization](1). For a K-injective resolution $I$, restriction to the open is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], since it is right adjoint to exact extension by zero [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek-adjunction, def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek]. Hence these section identities also give the canonical derived restriction identities and preserve the proper-composition coordinates of step 3. Restrict the unit/square/counit formula for $B_{h_a}$ to $X'$: the vertical maps become identities on $X$ and $X'$, the horizontal map is $u$, and the section formulas for the vertical unit and counit send a section to itself. The pullback square map becomes the identity of $u^*$, because both pullback composites are $u^*$. The formula therefore gives the identity of $u^*K$, not merely an unspecified isomorphism. The maps $e_{h_a},e_k,e_{k_a}$ restrict to identity by their defining uniqueness in [det-sf-comp-composition-interchange](2), and $O_a,O_d$ do so by step 1. Thus both $L_a$ and $M_a$ restrict to identity. Apply interchange (2) with $p=\mathrm{id}_{X'}$, $i=j_a'$ and dense compactification $X'\hookrightarrow W\xrightarrow{k_a}Z_a'$: after the isomorphism $O_a$ it gives $M_a=L_a$. This uniqueness application uses density of $W$, never density of $D'$.

Apply $Rp'_{a*}$ to $L_a=M_a$ and precompose with $B_{p_a,j_{a!}K}:v^*Rp_{a*}j_{a!}K\to Rp'_{a*}v_a^*j_{a!}K$. Naturality of $B_{p_a}$ in the morphism $e_{h_a}$ and the mate-pasting equation of step 3 for $q=p_ah_a$ identify the right-hand side with $\rho_k\beta_dv^*(\rho_{h_a})$. The left-hand side is $\rho_{k_a}\beta_{c_a}$. More explicitly the proper factors on the right are $(Rp'_{a*}B_{h_a})\circ(B_{p_a}Rh_{a*})=B_q$ by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2),(3); the open factors are $O_d$ followed by $e_k$, exactly those in $\rho_k\beta_d$. We have proved the typed equality of natural transformations
$$\rho_{k_a}\beta_{c_a}=\rho_k\beta_dv^*(\rho_{h_a}):v^*F_{c_a}\longrightarrow F_{d''}u^*.$$
The construction and section calculations are natural in $K$, so this is a functor-level equality.

statement_change.what: The imported statement omitted the standing scheme setting required by every coefficient, proper-base-change, extension, and coherence input. In particular the integral coefficient argument applies its proper-base-change clause to the base-changed proper map, so Y' must also be a standing scheme. The corrected statement states the global standing setting and makes v a morphism in it, preserving all three clauses and the source hypotheses.

citers.note: Its cartesian base-change clause is applied only for standing schemes, exactly the corrected setting.

old_proof.text:
*(1)* Both $v'^*j_!$ and $j'_!u^*$ are left adjoint to the same functor
$u_*j'^*\simeq j^*v'_*$ (restriction to an open commutes with direct image, as
in [det-sf-comp-coherence-single]); hence they are canonically isomorphic.
Concretely, both restrict to $u^*$ on the open $X'\subset\overline X'$ and vanish
on its closed complement, which characterizes extensions by zero (Stacks, Tag
09AH). Both functors are exact on sheaves, so the isomorphism passes to
derived categories termwise.

*(2)* The functor $v^*$ is exact, preserves direct sums and carries
$\Dctf(-,\Lambda)$ into $\Dctf(-,\Lambda)$ (flat constructible models for finite
rings, pulled-back local coefficient models otherwise), so it preserves
$\Loc(\Dctf(-,\Lambda))$; the same holds for $u^*$ and $v'^*$. For
$K\in\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))$ we have $j_!K\in\Loc(\Dctf(\overline X,\Lambda))$ by
[det-sf-comp-coherence-single], so proper base change for $p$ along $v$ on
the localizing category ([sk-prop-proper-base-change-unbounded]) gives
$v^*Rp_*j_!K\simeq Rp'_*v'^*j_!K$, and (1) gives $Rp'_*v'^*j_!K\simeq Rp'_*j'_!u^*K$.

*(3)* Let $h:Z'\to Z$ be a refinement of dense compactifications of $f$, with
base change $h':Z'_{Y'}\to Z_{Y'}$, a refinement of compactifications of $f'$
(not necessarily dense; [det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle] allows dense
replacement). The two composites $v^*Rp_*j_!K\to Rp'_*Rh'_*j''_!u^*K$ obtained
by first comparing compactifications and then base changing, or conversely,
are both obtained by applying $Rp'_*$ to maps
$v_Z^*j_!K\to Rh'_*j''_!u^*K$ which restrict to the identity of $u^*K$ over the
open $X'$ (the refinement maps and the isomorphism (1) restrict to identities,
and proper base change for $h$ is compatible with restriction to the open
$X'$ on which $h'$ is the identity). By adjunction for the open immersion,
such a map is unique, so the two composites agree; hence $\beta$ is
independent of the compactification.
